articles.title: IHC tells Adiala jail authorities to ensure Imran, Bushra Bibi are not kept in solitary confinement
articles.description: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Monday declared petitions challenging the alleged solitary confinement of PTI founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi maintainable and also directed Adiala jail authorities to ensure that neither was kept in solitary confinement. IHC’s Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro announced the verdict, which had been reserved on Aug 6, and held that the petitions were maintainable in light of the principles laid down in the Begum Nusrat Bhutto and Begum Shamim Afridi cases. The court also directed jail authorities to facilitate a meeting between Imran and Bushra in accordance with prison rules. It further ordered that Imran’s family members be allowed to meet him as permitted under the jail rules and directed authorities to make arrangements for telephone conversations between him and his sons. More to follow

articles.title: Trump's 'mafia state' move exposed the rotten core of his latest oil deal: expert
articles.description: President Donald Trump just pulled off what one political expert described as a "mafia state" type of move that revealed the rotten core of a deal he allegedly struck with a foreign country over its oil reserves. Trump recently announced that the U.S. and North American Blue Energy Partners , a private company led by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt, entered into a partnership to tap Venezuela's 65 billion barrel oil reserves, a deal that is estimated to be worth tens of billions of dollars. Betancourt was previously under investigation on corruption charges until Trump's former attorney, Rudy Giuliani , persuaded the first Trump Department of Justice to drop its probe. David Rothkopf, global affairs columnist at The Daily Beast and a former international trade official in the Clinton administration, argued during a new episode of "The Daily Beast Podcast," that the "deal" Trump announced is not a deal at all. "The United States is getting this all because we attacked Venezuela and at gunpoint are saying, 'Hand over the oil!' That's illegal under international law," Rothkopf said. "It's also ... illegal under Venezuelan law, which has a constitution that says you can't hand over reserves to a foreign government. It's probably illegal under U.S. law because it involves cash flowing into the U.S. government ... which requires congressional approval." Rothkopf drew a comparison between the Trump administration's move to seize Venezuela's oil and the way Russia's government operates, arguing that the Trump administration will break laws and customs without regard. "It's a crime," Rothkopf said. "It's not a deal."

articles.title: Protest in New York against RSS chief’s visit
articles.description: WASHINGTON: A large demonstration erupted outside Madison Square Garden this week as Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh chief Mohan Bhagwat attended an event billed as a celebration of “Universal Oneness”, with protesters saying the message contradicted the RSS’s Hindu supremacist ideology. Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Dalit and civil-rights groups converged outside the New York landmark to protest Bhagwat’s appearance, accusing the RSS of promoting a majoritarian vision of India and of being associated with violence and discrimination against religious minorities. The demonstration took place as thousands of people gathered inside the venue for the “Universal Oneness Celebration”, organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue. Organisers presented the event as a celebration of Hindu culture and the idea of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — the world as one family. But protesters said universal brotherhood placards could not conceal what they described as the RSS’s record in India. “This is kind of a goodwill tour to improve the public image of the RSS,” Sravya Tadepalli of Hindus for Human Rights told reporters before the event, des­cribing the organisation as a “fascist paramilitary organisation” accused of decades of communal violence against minorities. The protest was organised under the banner “Hindus Say No to the RSS”, with organisers calling for a secular and interfaith India. The coalition said the RSS’s Hindu nationalist vision threatens Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Dalits and others who do not fit its conception of the Indian nation. The opposition had gathered momentum well before Bhagwat reached New York. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani publicly opposed the event, describing the rise of what he called an exclusionary vision of India as deeply troubling. He said the city might not have legal authority to stop a privately organised event. The controversy also reached Washington. The US Commission on International Religious Freedom called for Bhagwat’s visa to be revoked and urged the Trump administration to consider targeted sanctions against RSS members and Indian officials. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

articles.title: Supreme Court Lets Trump Continue Building His Tacky Ballroom
articles.description: A divided Supreme Court on Monday allowed President Trump to continue construction on his White House ballroom. In a 5–4 decision that broke somewhat along traditional ideological lines, the court granted an emergency request filed by the Trump administration to proceed with construction on the president’s controversial plans for a White House ballroom. Justice John Roberts joined all three of the court’s liberal justices in dissenting. “Construction of the ballroom has proceeded apace for the better part of a year,” Roberts wrote on behalf of the four dissenting justices. “That construction is likely unlawful. Pursuant to its ple nary constitutional authority over the District of Columbia and federal property, Congress has explicitly prohibited the construction of any ‘building or structure ... on any reservation, park, or public grounds of the Federal Government in the District of Columbia without express authority of Congress.” ... The ballroom is a building or structure being erected on federal park grounds—President’s Park—in the District of Columbia. Yet Congress has not passed any law resembling ‘express authority’ for the Executive’s construction of it.” This is a developing story.

articles.title: Trump rages that angry towns defying his key priority will wind up 'backwards and poor'
articles.description: President Donald Trump took to social media Monday to lash out at “communities throughout the U.S.A.” for resisting his administration’s nationwide data center push , a key priority of the White House that has been largely rejected by Americans. “The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centers is if they want to end up being backwards and poor. If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign,” Trump wrote on his social media platform Truth Social. “The good news is that there are plenty of other places that want them. If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame. China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement. Actually, they can’t believe it is happening!” In July 2025, Trump signed an executive order to accelerate permits for data center construction. In the months since, construction on data centers has ramped up across the country. Meanwhile, Americans have grown to oppose the construction of data centers, with a new poll conducted by Embold Research suggesting that a staggering 75% of Americans were opposed to a new data center being built in their community.
